title: Future value of an annuity
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank points either build an annuity's total as a geometric series or cover using interest factor tables for both future and present value, so none is exactly the future value of an annuity from tables or a spreadsheet.

draft.title: Future value of an annuity
card: The future value of an annuity is the total it grows to, including every payment and all the interest earned. Interest is paid on each payment from the day it goes in.
A table of future value interest factors gives a number for each interest rate per period and number of periods. The rate and periods must match how often payments are made.
Future value = payment × factor. A spreadsheet can also give the answer.
Example: $200 is paid in at the end of each year for 3 years at 5% p.a. The factor for 5% and 3 periods is 3.1525. Future value = 200 × 3.1525 = $630.50.
draft.remember: Future value = payment × table factor, using the rate and periods that match each payment.

a.q: An annuity pays $500 at the end of each year. For its rate and term, the future value factor is 4.3101. What is the future value?
a.why: Future value = 500 × 4.3101 = $2155.05. Dividing by the factor gives a much smaller number, because the factor is a multiplier that includes interest. That is a common mistake.
a.clue: Multiply the payment by the factor.

b.q: Leila saves $300 at the end of each quarter for 2 years at 8% p.a. compounded quarterly. Which factor should she use from the table?
b.why: Payments are quarterly, so the rate is 8% ÷ 4 = 2% per quarter. Two years has 2 × 4 = 8 quarters, so there are 8 periods. Using 8% and 2 periods matches the yearly figures, not the quarterly payments.
b.clue: Change both the rate and the term to quarters.

check.summary: No problems found. The example factor (3.1525 for 5% over 3 periods) and both answers ($2155.05; 2% per period for 8 periods) check out.
